title: Validate against GH #1 success criteria on the 20260729 and 20260817 recordings
description: Run the full pipeline on both recordings (OneDrive canonical paths; 20260729 = Soso_20260729_class_audio.m4a, 60:51; 20260817 = 56:00). Compare merged transcripts to work/ref-windowed references; check every item in the epic's acceptance list; run a <20-min recording (or a 15-min clip) both windowed and --window-minutes 0 and confirm the moments agree. Record run counts, wall-clock and token usage per window in the issue notes.
acceptance_criteria: All epic acceptance criteria checked off with evidence pasted into notes; 10/10 consecutive Pass A successes on one 60-min recording.

title: P2: stream watchdog in generate(): inactivity timeout + repetition-loop detector + retry with temperature bump
description: gemini.py generate(): (a) abort the attempt if no chunk arrives for ~120 s (the 2026-08-17 hang streamed slowly for 40 min and defeated the 30-min HTTP timeout); (b) on the accumulated tail (last ~2000 chars) detect a short cycle (≤64-char substring covering >80% of the tail) and raise RepetitionLoop immediately; (c) both are retryable per window — on loop-retry use temperature 0.5 for that attempt, then restore; (d) re-add the finish_reason==MAX_TOKENS diagnostic + partial dump from work/thinking-budget-attempt.patch as the backstop. Unit-test the detector on work/20260729/pass_a_partial.attempt1.json (real 58k-char 「持っ、」 loop) and on a clean window transcript (no false positive).
acceptance_criteria: Detector fires on the 20260729 loop partial within the first ~2k chars of garbage and never on the three ref-windowed 20260817 transcripts; a simulated stalled stream aborts in ~2 min; retries are per-window.
notes: Reproduced cleanly while doing jld-hc9.2 (2026-08-20), and it is a first-chunk stall, not a mid-stream one: generate_content_stream on a 24 s audio window + response_schema never delivered chunk 0 in 5 of 6 attempts, each sitting in _ssl__SSLSocket_read (verified with macOS sample on the live process) until killed at 5-7 min — while a plain text stream on the same client answered in 2.5 s and one earlier attempt on the SAME clip returned 7 chunks in 13 s. So the watchdog must start its clock at request time, not at first byte, or it will never fire on this case. Repro: uv run distill run work/test/test_lesson.m4a --date <new> --work-dir work/hc9-2-verify --skip-pass-b --window-minutes 0.4 --overlap-seconds 8. Probes kept nothing behind; the three real 20-min windows of the 2026-08-17 lesson never stalled, so short audio may be the trigger — check whether thinking_level (jld-hc9.1) changes it before building elaborate retry logic.

title: P3: pin model explicitly and migrate thinking_budget → thinking_level
description: gemini.py/pipeline.py: default model becomes an explicit pin (e.g. gemini-3.1-pro) instead of the gemini-pro-latest alias; Pass A sends thinking_config=ThinkingConfig(thinking_level='low') (transcription is mechanical); detect/Pass B keep default. Never send thinking_budget and thinking_level together (400). Log thoughts_token_count vs requested level each call; warn when missing (None) or far above expectation. google-genai 2.11.0 already supports thinking_level.
acceptance_criteria: One instrumented Pass A window with thinking_level=low shows thoughts_token_count in the low thousands, not ~60k; model name in moments.json is the pinned id.

title: P1: window Pass A internally (split → per-window transcribe → offset-shift → overlap de-dup)
description: audio.py: split_windows(audio, win_s=20*60, overlap_s=30) -> [(path, offset_s)] via ffmpeg stream copy into work/<date>/windows/. pipeline.py Pass A: transcribe each window separately, cache per window (transcript_w01.json …) so a failed window retries alone; shift every segment start by the window offset; concatenate; in each overlap region keep window N up to the overlap midpoint and window N+1 after it. Keep transcript.json as the final merged output so detect/Pass B/emit are untouched. Expose --window-minutes/--overlap-seconds on the CLI (0 = single pass, for the <20-min regression check).
acceptance_criteria: uv run distill run on the 20260817 recording completes Pass A without manual staging; merged transcript covers 00:00-56:00; diff against work/ref-windowed/*/20260817/transcript.json (offsets 0/1140/2340) shows the same content at the same absolute times; no duplicate segments across overlaps.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: audio.window_starts/split_windows + pipeline._pass_a/merge_windows, CLI --window-minutes/--overlap-seconds, ADR-0005, 12 offline tests. Real run on the 20260817 recording (no manual staging): 3 windows at 0/19:30/39:00, 437 merged segments, last at 55:56 of 56:00, monotonic, no duplicate segments across seams, no empty 5-min stretch; all 313 reference lines from work/ref-windowed/ present at the same absolute times (260 matched in place, 53 within seconds but re-attributed — see the diarization bug jld-dli). ~5 min wall clock vs ~30 for the single-call version, which stopped at 49:59. Re-run with windows cached made zero API calls.

title: Pass A reliability on ~60-min recordings: windowed Pass A + stream watchdog + Gemini 3 thinking migration
description: Single-pass Pass A on a ~60-min lesson fails 4/6 and silently drops content on its 'successes' (GH #1 investigation, GH #2 spike: https://github.com/srsaito/jp-lesson-distill/issues/2). Root cause: one constrained-decoding generation of a 30-70k-token JSON transcript is outside the model's reliable envelope; thinking_budget is a no-op on Gemini 3.1 Pro (gemini-pro-latest moved 2026-03-06). Fix = build the manual 3-window rescue into the pipeline plus containment. Reference data: work/ref-windowed/w{1,2,3}/<date>/transcript.json (known-good windowed transcripts for 20260729 and 20260817, offsets in offset.txt). Prior no-op attempt saved as work/thinking-budget-attempt.patch (its MAX_TOKENS diagnostic is worth re-adding).
acceptance_criteria: GH #1 success criteria: 10/10 clean Pass A runs on a 60-min recording; 600-800 segments/hour; 「静かった」 at ~27:26 on 20260729; 上旬/中旬/下旬 and 好きの→好きな present for 20260817 (19:30-25:30); hesitation clip (20260729 35:00-36:30, 「持っ、」) does not loop or aborts in seconds; Pass B clips audibly contain student_verbatim; short (<20 min) recording gives same moments windowed vs single-pass.

title: Address-form consistency as a free per-run diarization canary in quality.py
description: Diarization quality varies run-to-run on identical input (jld-dli), and ground truth is expensive — ~15 minutes of Steven's listening per lesson, and it only ever covers one lesson after the fact. There is a check that costs nothing and needs no ground truth and no extra API call: address forms pin a speaker regardless of voice. Only Soso先生 says 「スティーブンさん」 or 「奥さん」 (someone else's wife); only Steven says 「先生」 as an address or 「妻」 (his own wife). Counting how often a segment's label agrees with the address form inside it separated the two 2026-08-17 runs cleanly BEFORE any listening was done: windowed run 8/9 = 89%, hand-staged reference 3/8 = 38%, and hand-staged w1 alone 1/5. Had this been in quality.py, the bad run would have been flagged at the time and jld-dli would have started from the right premise instead of the wrong one. marker_conflict() in labeling.py already implements the per-segment test.
acceptance_criteria: quality.py reports address-form agreement per window alongside coverage/dead-time/max-span; it WARNS and never fails, because the marker count is small (about 9 lines an hour, and a window can legitimately contain zero). Verified against the known-good windowed run and the known-bad hand-staged reference in work/ref-windowed/.
notes: Warn-only is deliberate and matters: with roughly 3 marker lines per 20-minute window, 1 disagreement is not evidence of anything, so a gate here would either fire constantly or never. Its value is as a trend line across lessons — a run at 40% is worth a listening kit, a run at 90% is not. Reuse labeling.MARKERS and labeling.marker_conflict rather than restating the list, so the ground-truth kit and the gate can never drift apart. Note the cue is sparse by nature and a lesson heavy on textbook drills may have almost none; report the denominator, never just the percentage.
close_reason: Built. quality.py now counts address-form agreement per window (reported in the stats line, warn-only above MARKER_MIN_N=4) and pipeline.py prints a whole-run verdict after the merge, where the hour's ~9 cues make a usable denominator. Verified on both real 2026-08-17 runs: windowed 8/9 'consistent', hand-staged 3/8 'looks unreliable' naming distill label as the next step. test_the_bad_run_is_caught_here_and_nowhere_else asserts the key property — hand-staged w1 passes coverage, dead-time, span and monotonicity while scoring 1/5 here. 14 new tests, 73 total, all passing.

title: Pass A merges two speakers into one segment ~12% of the time (segmentation, not diarization)
description: Blind ground truth on the 2026-08-17 lesson (jld-dli, 2026-08-25) found 5 of 41 sampled segments whose TEXT spans two turns — Steven's line and Soso先生's run together in a single segment with a single speaker label. That is 12% of the sample, and it is now the largest measured defect in Pass A output: genuine teacher/student swaps were 1 in 36. No speaker label can be correct for a merged turn, so these are silently excluded from any accuracy figure and quietly flatter it. They also break the two things downstream depends on: detect reads a merged segment as one person saying both the error and the correction, and Pass B clips +/-15 s around a start time that now belongs to the wrong speaker's turn. Four of the five cluster in 51:01-52:43, a fast correction exchange ('入らない' vs 'いらない'), plus one at 30:54 — i.e. the failure mode is rapid back-and-forth, exactly where the learning moments are. quality.py's under-split check is about a single long turn and does not see this.
acceptance_criteria: A measured merged-turn rate on a second lesson, and either a Pass A prompt change that reduces it or a post-hoc splitter, verified against the 2026-08-17 ground truth in tests/fixtures/diarization_truth_20260817.json (5 known merged segments, timestamps included). AND the vault skill .claude/commands/distill-jp-lesson.md section 1b is updated to match — it quotes the 12% figure and tells the card agent to hand-check suspect segments, both of which go stale when this ships.
notes: SHIP STEP — DO NOT CLOSE WITHOUT IT: update the vault skill /Users/stevensaito/Docs/Vault-GeneralNotes/.claude/commands/distill-jp-lesson.md, section '1b. Check WHO the transcript says was speaking'. It currently tells the card-generating agent that ~12% of segments merge two speakers, that the merge clusters in fast correction exchanges, and that a student_verbatim which appears to contain its own correction should be quoted as suspect and checked against the transcript by hand. When this lands, replace that with the real behaviour: whether merged turns are now split, merely flagged, or still present at a lower rate — and give the new measured rate, since the 12% figure is quoted in the skill and will go stale. If the fix is a post-hoc splitter, say what it does to timestamps, because the skill quotes [MM:SS] into the lesson note and Pass B clips +/-15 s around those starts.

title: Pass A has no label for played textbook audio — Soso先生's playbacks are transcribed as his own speech
description:
Segment.speaker is Literal[teacher, student], but a third thing speaks in these lessons: Soso先生 plays the textbook audio (Z_audio_L##/*.mp3) during class, typically twice per dialogue. Those playbacks are currently transcribed as teacher speech.

Evidence already collected by Steven in OneDrive .../日本語/Soso/Vol 3/L13/Z_kaiwa_scripts_L13.md: in 20260729-transcript.md, 会話13-08 was played at [42:22][42:39][43:06] and again at [44:32][44:49][45:16]; 会話13-09 at [49:11][49:44] and [50:53][51:26]. Cross-checked against a Gemini transcription of the source mp3s, the lesson transcript matches the textbook audio verbatim apart from two orthographic variants (様々／さまざま, こちらタオルです／こちら、タオルです).

Why it matters, in order of cost:
1. detect sees fluent native sentences attributed to the teacher and can mine them as new-item candidates, producing cards from textbook audio rather than from the lesson.
2. jld-dli's repair pass will try to re-attribute these lines using fluency and address-form cues, which is exactly wrong — nobody in the room said them.
3. A student repetition right after a playback loses its context: the thing being repeated looks like teacher speech.

Also documented there: 会話13-07's playback is MISSING from the transcript entirely — [34:22]「じゃあまず聞きましょう」 then 73 seconds of nothing until [35:35]. So Pass A sometimes transcribes played audio and sometimes silently drops it. That 73 s hole is the kind of thing jld-hc9.4's dead-time gate now flags, but a retry may not fix it if the model systematically skips playback.

Options: add a third speaker value (schema change, touches detect and emit — probably wants an ADR); or keep the binary label and mark playback spans separately via a flag on Segment; or detect playback acoustically by matching the lesson audio against Z_audio_L##/*.mp3, which is model-free and also gives exact spans.
acceptance_criteria: Playback spans in a real lesson are identified and excluded from moment detection and from any diarization repair; a decision recorded on whether that means a new speaker value, a span flag, or acoustic matching. AND the vault skill .claude/commands/distill-jp-lesson.md section 1b is updated to match — it currently instructs the card agent to spot playback by hand, and that instruction becomes wrong the moment this ships.
notes: SHIP STEP — DO NOT CLOSE WITHOUT IT: update the vault skill /Users/stevensaito/Docs/Vault-GeneralNotes/.claude/commands/distill-jp-lesson.md, section '1b. Check WHO the transcript says was speaking'. That section currently tells the card-generating agent to spot played textbook audio BY HAND, using the tell 'a contiguous run of teacher segments containing a two-role exchange with no student line in between', and warns that a moment sourced from playback must not become a card about Steven's error. Once this issue lands, that manual instruction is wrong and should be replaced with whatever the implementation actually gives the agent — a 'played' speaker value, a span flag on the transcript, or a field on the moment. Say explicitly whether moments from played audio are now excluded upstream or still need filtering, because the agent will otherwise keep hand-filtering and may double-drop. Same for the vault card rules in _wiki/日本語の授業/CLAUDE.md if the moment schema changes shape.

title: Pass A diarization is unstable run-to-run: 71% teacher/student agreement between two runs of the same lesson
description: Two independent Gemini Pass A runs over the 2026-08-17 lesson (the hand-staged work/ref-windowed/ windows and the windowed run in work/hc9-2-verify/20260817/) transcribe the same words but disagree on WHO SAID THEM for 76 of 260 matched lines — 71% agreement. Examples, ref label vs windowed-run label: 03:04 student/teacher 「あー、私も牛肉のシュニッツェルは食べたことがありません、だと思います」 (the tacked-on だと思います reads learner, so the run is likely wrong); 07:01 student/teacher 「でも、今週末はあんまり暑くない予報、予想？」; 08:06 student/teacher; 09:30 teacher/student 「あー、行った方がいいです」. Not a windowing artifact — the disagreements sit deep inside window 1 in both runs, and merge_windows never touches the speaker field. Matters because detect keys off diarization: an uncorrected-error attributed to the teacher is invisible, and a teacher line attributed to the student is a false candidate. Worth measuring against ground truth (listen to a dozen contested spots) before deciding whether the fix is a stronger prompt, an explicit voice description, or a diarization repair pass over adjacent turns.
acceptance_criteria: A measured teacher/student accuracy figure against hand-labeled ground truth on ~30 contested lines, and a decision (with rationale) on whether Pass A prompting changes or a repair pass follows.
notes: ERRATUM to the note above: the canary issue is jld-86b, not jld-ktm (I cited the id before creating it).
close_reason: Acceptance met: teacher/student accuracy measured against blind hand-labelled ground truth (32/36 = 89% overall, 18/19 = 95% on the random stratum), and the decision is no repair pass and no Pass A prompt change — the diarization contributes 1 error in 36. The run-to-run instability was real, but the reference run was the broken one (0/16 on contested lines, p=3e-5). The remaining error budget is filed: jld-lg6 (played textbook audio, 3 of the 4 errors) and jld-beb (merged turns, 5/41, now the largest defect).

title: ADR: windowed Pass A + explicit model pinning (amends ADR-0002); update hot.md/README; close GH #1 and #2
description: Write decisions/0005-windowed-pass-a-and-model-pinning.md (MADR-lite): context = GH #1/#2 evidence; decision = 20-min/30-s windows, explicit model pin with deliberate upgrades, thinking_level=low for Pass A, watchdog + gates; consequences = alias drift no longer silently changes production behaviour; cost/latency notes from validation. Update hot.md (remove the 'thinking_budget' lesson, record the new operating envelope), README/architecture.md Pass A description, then close GH #1 and #2 with a pointer to the ADR.
acceptance_criteria: ADR committed and indexed in decisions/README.md; hot.md reflects the new state; GH #1 and #2 closed.
notes: Partly done by jld-hc9.2 (2026-08-20): decisions/0005-windowed-pass-a.md is written and indexed, and hot.md / README.md / docs/architecture.md / CLAUDE.md already describe windowed Pass A. Deliberately scoped to windowing only — the model-pinning and thinking_level half belongs with jld-hc9.1, so this issue's remainder is: fold pinning + thinking_level into an ADR (amend 0005 or add 0006), record the validated cost/latency envelope from jld-hc9.5, and close GH #1 and #2 pointing at it. Latency datum to reuse: 3x20-min windows on the 2026-08-17 lesson = ~5 min wall clock total, vs ~30 min for the old single hour-long call.

title: P4: per-window sanity gates on Pass A output (density, monotonic timestamps, coverage, max segment length)
description: After each window: last segment start within ~90 s of window end; timestamps non-decreasing; ≥ ~8 segments per audio-minute (good runs ~11/min, degraded ≤7/min); no segment text > ~300 chars (degraded runs produced a 1,153-char segment absorbing 7 min). Gate failure = retry the window (counts toward the same retry budget as P2). Print the per-window stats so degradation is visible in the run log.
acceptance_criteria: Feeding the single-pass work/20260817/transcript.json through the gates as if it were one window fails on coverage (49:59 vs 56:00) and density; all three ref-windowed 20260817 transcripts pass.
notes:
Measured all Pass A transcripts on disk 2026-08-21 to calibrate the gates. Density does not work; three other signals do. Table (seg/min | longest span one segment must cover | count >60s | 'dead time' = audio inside spans carrying <1 char/sec | exact duplicate texts >20 chars):

  ref w1 (good)       8.8 |  42s | 0 | 0.0m |  0
  ref w2 (good)       4.6 |  74s | 1 | 0.0m |  1
  ref w3 (good)       6.9 |  41s | 0 | 0.0m |  0
  0817 windowed       7.8 |  45s | 0 | 0.0m |  2
  0817 single (BAD)   7.0 | 361s | 3 | 8.1m | 31
  0707 single         5.5 | 171s | 3 | 1.7m | 11

- SEGMENTS/MIN DOES NOT SEPARATE: the known-bad transcript (7.0) sits between known-good ones (4.6 to 9.6). Nor does chars/min (bad 177, good 162-205). Drop the >=8/min gate or demote it to a logged statistic.
- MAX SPAN separates cleanly: good windows top out at 42-74 s; the bad one has a single segment covering 361 s. The Pass A prompt already says split turns at ~30 s, so >60 s is a prompt violation, not a judgement call.
- DEAD TIME separates cleanly: 0 min on every good transcript, 8.1 min on the bad one. Concrete instance: [11:20] teacher 「うん。いいですね。」 — 9 characters asked to cover 64 seconds of audio. This is the silent-compression detector the epic wanted.
- COVERAGE remains the strongest single gate: 89% vs 100%.
- DUPLICATES ARE AMBIGUOUS, warn only. In the bad 0817 run they are the mechanism of failure: four consecutive lines from 11:13-13:04 re-emitted verbatim at 20:12-21:03, i.e. the model lost its place and replayed an earlier block over eight minutes of real audio. But 0707's 11 duplicates are three passes over the same textbook dialogue (「木村さん、ネットでパソコン買ったことありますか？」 at 40:35, 43:40, 44:58) — a genuine classroom drill, correctly transcribed. Structurally the two look alike, so duplicate blocks must warn, never auto-fail; coverage and dead time are what tell them apart. Note the windowed run's 2 duplicates are also genuine (the roleplay line repeated 55 s later).
- 0707 is NOT degraded despite failing the proposed density and 300-char gates: its long segment is 590 chars over 171 s = 3.5 chars/sec, i.e. continuous speech that was merely under-split. A raw character-count gate would have failed a good run; span and yield are the right measures.
close_reason: Implemented as src/jp_lesson_distill/quality.py + wiring in _pass_a. Gates that fail a window and buy a retry at higher temperature: coverage, monotonic, dead-time (audio in spans under 1 char/s), max-span (>180s). Warn-only: density floor, under-split turns, duplicates. Density is logged but NOT gated — measured proof it cannot work is in the tests (the known-bad run is denser than a known-good window). Attempts kept as transcript_w<NN>.attempt<N>.json; least-bad promoted with a warning if all fail. --window-attempts (default 2). Acceptance criterion met: the single-pass work/20260817/transcript.json fails on coverage (49:59 of 56:00) and dead-time (486s, 14%) and max-span (361s); all three ref-windowed transcripts pass, as do all three windows of the good windowed run. 25 offline tests pass; verified end-to-end on the cached 20260817 windows (stats line per window, duplicate warning correctly fires on the roleplay repetitions without failing the window).

value: thinking_budget is a no-op on Gemini 3.x (gemini-pro-latest → 3.1 Pro since 2026-03-06); use thinking_level. Single-pass Pass A on ~60-min audio is unreliable AND silently lossy even when it 'succeeds' — always window (~20 min). Known-good windowed reference transcripts: work/ref-windowed/w{1,2,3}/<date>/ (offset.txt = seconds). See GH #1/#2 and epic jld-hc9.
